text: The Fed held rates at 3.75–4% in a 10-2 vote; two officials wanted a quarter-point hike, and futures put the odds of a December hike at about 83%.
Gold finished flat near $4,057 after dipping to about $4,035 right after the decision; silver fell about 1.1% to $53.72, pushing the gold/silver ratio above 75.5.
The 10-year yield rose about 3 bp to near 5.03% while the 2-year fell about 3 bp to near 4.70% during the Fed chair's press conference.
Stocks rose for a third day: the S&P 500 gained 0.28% to 7,743.98 and the Nasdaq 0.27% to 26,549.85. QQQ closed up 0.6% at $725.61.
After the bell, Alphabet fell about 10% as heavy AI spending turned its free cash flow negative, while Microsoft rose on a revenue and earnings beat.
Gold miners held up better than gold: GDX closed up 0.9% at $83.95 while gold was flat.
Brent touched about $116.50 on Middle East supply fears before trimming gains; reports of the settle disagree ($111–$115), so Brent is left blank this update.
Bitcoin briefly hit about $81,700 after the decision, then slipped back to about $79,700, down 1.4% over 24 hours.
